artists.name: Yazoo
artists.blurb: Days after leaving Depeche Mode, Vince Clarke teamed up with Alison Moyet. Two perfect albums — Upstairs at Eric's and You and Me Both — and singles like Only You and Don't Go.

artists.name: The Assembly
artists.blurb: Vince Clarke and Blackwing engineer Eric Radcliffe's one-single project: Never Never, sung by Feargal Sharkey, reached the UK top 5.

artists.name: Erasure
artists.blurb: Vince found Andy Bell through a Melody Maker ad and never looked back — 40 years, 19 albums, and some of the greatest pop songs Britain has produced.

artists.name: Recoil
artists.blurb: Alan Wilder's experimental outlet, which became his main vehicle after leaving Depeche Mode in 1995 — cinematic, sample-driven records like Unsound Methods and subHuman.

artists.name: Dave Gahan & Soulsavers
artists.blurb: Dave's solo records Paper Monsters and Hourglass proved the voice could write too, and his ongoing collaboration with Soulsavers found gospel-soaked gold.

artists.name: Martin L. Gore
artists.blurb: Martin's Counterfeit cover EPs and instrumental electronic albums (MG, The Third Chimpanzee) — the songwriter exploring everyone else's songs, and no songs at all.

artists.name: VCMG
artists.blurb: Thirty years after Vince left, Clarke and Gore reunited for Ssss — a pure techno album made almost entirely by swapping files, barely meeting in person. Very them.
